solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Stays in my place (6)

blocks.note: 'My!' and 'Cor!' are both exclamations of surprise
to set = to place

annotation.surface: Someone declines to move, staying put where they belong.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stays' reads as a verb, but it is the old noun for a boned corset. 'My' is not the possessive but the exclamation, as in 'My, what a surprise!'
annotation.definitionFit: A corset was traditionally called a pair of stays, after the stiffening strips sewn into it.

entries.clue: Angry about combination of two different styles (9)

blocks.note: cross = angry
over = about, as in 'a row over money'

annotation.surface: Someone is annoyed at a fusion of two musical or fashion styles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of 'angry about', but it supplies OVER, in the sense of 'concerning'.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossover is a work that blends two genres, such as a country-pop record.

entries.clue: Followers to join up on borders (7)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, 'up' means the word is written from the bottom
indicatorNotes.borders: RE borders the rest, sitting on either side of it

blocks.note: re = on, concerning
to unite = to join, written upwards as ETINU

annotation.surface: A leader's supporters are told to band together at the frontiers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Borders' looks like a noun meaning frontiers, but it is a verb: the word for 'on' sits at both edges of the upturned join.
annotation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants who follow an important person.

entries.clue: Regret climbing competition lacking base in continent (6)

indicatorNotes.climbing: in a down entry, climbing means the word reads from the bottom up
indicatorNotes.lacking base: the base of a down entry is its last letter, which goes

blocks.note: RUE = regret, written upwards
OPEN, a golf or tennis tournament, without its last letter N

annotation.surface: Someone is sorry that a mountaineering contest lost its base camp on some continent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Climbing competition' looks like one phrase about mountaineering; 'climbing' belongs to 'Regret' before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Europe is one of the seven continents usually counted.

entries.clue: Revelling in macho hairstyle (7)

indicatorNotes.Revelling: revelling suggests letters partying wildly, so they rearrange

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A tough guy's haircut is part of his partying.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word joining 'Revelling' to 'macho', but it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A Mohican is a hairstyle with the sides shaved and a central strip left standing, called a mohawk in the US.

entries.clue: Man discards shirt at last — tight one (5)

indicatorNotes.discards: discards means a letter is thrown out
indicatorNotes.at last: at last picks the final letter of 'shirt'

blocks.note: mister = man, as a form of address
the last letter of shirT, removed from MISTER

annotation.surface: A man takes off his shirt because it is too tight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tight' sounds like a fit of clothing, keeping the shirt picture, but here it is slang for stingy.
annotation.definitionFit: A tight person is mean with money, so a tight one is a miser.

entries.clue: Respect checking record for beginning of site visit? (4,4)

indicatorNotes.checking: to check is to hold back or restrain, so HOMAGE holds EP

blocks.note: homage = respect
EP = extended-play record, placed after HOM

annotation.surface: Showing reverence while checking a register before visiting a site.
annotation.walkthrough: HOM(EP)AGE. The question mark flags a playful definition: a website visit usually begins on its home page.
annotation.definitionFit: The home page is the first page you land on when visiting a website.

entries.clue: Comfort individual supporting prisoner (7)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down entry, the supporting piece sits underneath

blocks.note: con = convict
sole = single, individual

annotation.surface: A lone visitor stands by a prisoner to cheer him up.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces come in the reverse of clue order: SOLE supports CON, so it goes below.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: both mean to ease someone's grief or disappointment.

entries.clue: Old language found in Cameroon or Senegal (5)

indicatorNotes.found in: the answer is found inside the words that follow

blocks.note: cameroON OR SEnegal

annotation.surface: An ancient tongue is discovered in one of two West African countries.
annotation.walkthrough: The African setting leads away from Scandinavia, where Old Norse was spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: Old Norse is the medieval language of the Vikings, and Norse alone names it.

entries.clue: Rest before meal, ignoring large drink (3,5)

indicatorNotes.before: in a down entry, before means above
indicatorNotes.ignoring: ignoring means the letter for 'large' is left out

blocks.note: rump = the remainder, what is left
LUNCH without L, the abbreviation for large

annotation.surface: Advice to take a nap before eating and to skip the big drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rest' suggests a nap, but it means the remainder, as in the rump of a parliament.
annotation.definitionFit: Rum punch is a mixed drink of rum, fruit juice and spice.

entries.clue: Swimmer’s excessive gear regularly pruned (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly pruned: cutting back at regular intervals keeps every other letter

blocks.note: OTT = over the top
the even letters of gEaR

annotation.surface: A swimmer has too much kit, which gets trimmed back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer’s' reads as possessive, but the ’s is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The otter is a semi-aquatic mammal and a strong swimmer.

entries.clue: Unusual red star initially key for constellation (4,5)

indicatorNotes.initially: initially takes the first letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: the first letters of Unusual Red Star
A minor is a musical key

annotation.surface: A strange red star is at first the key to a star pattern.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' looks like an anagram indicator, but only its first letter is used. 'Key' supplies a whole key signature, A MINOR.
annotation.definitionFit: Ursa Minor, the Little Bear, is the constellation containing the Pole Star.

entries.clue: Tool packs seed for bird (9)

indicatorNotes.packs: packs means holds inside, as a case packs goods

blocks.note: a sander is a power tool for smoothing wood
a pip is a seed, inserted after SAND

annotation.surface: A garden tool is loaded with seed to feed the birds.
annotation.walkthrough: SAND(PIP)ER.
annotation.definitionFit: The sandpiper is a wading bird of shores and mudflats.

entries.clue: Subject lying face down (5)

blocks.note: an adjective here, as in 'subject to colds': liable to
the posture word, the opposite of supine

annotation.surface: Someone under examination lies face down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a noun but is the adjective, as in 'subject to colds'.
annotation.definitionFit: Prone means both liable to something and lying face down.

entries.clue: Change in direction ever changing (4)

indicatorNotes.changing: changing means the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A course that keeps shifting direction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Change' in the definition and 'changing' in the wordplay echo each other, so the whole clue seems to say one thing twice.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: a veer is a sudden swerve off course, as sailors use it of the wind.

entries.clue: Expert stops entry happening (2,8)

indicatorNotes.stops: to stop a hole is to fill it, so PRO plugs INGRESS

blocks.note: ingress = entry
pro = professional, expert, placed after IN

annotation.surface: A specialist blocks an entrance while something goes on.
annotation.walkthrough: IN(PRO)GRESS. 'Stops' looks like 'prevents', but it means plugs, as in stopping a gap.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: work under way and not yet finished is still going on, the adjectival sense of 'happening'.

entries.clue: Downgrade extremely reliable ambassador (8)

indicatorNotes.extremely: extremely takes the letters at the extremes of the word

blocks.note: the outer letters of ReliablE
a legate is an envoy, especially a papal one

annotation.surface: A thoroughly dependable diplomat is demoted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'reliable', but it keeps only its ends.
annotation.definitionFit: To relegate is to move to a lower rank or division.

entries.clue: Town flat in the middle of play area (9)

indicatorNotes.in the middle of: EVEN goes in the middle of STAGE

blocks.note: the stage is where a play is performed
even = flat, level, placed after ST

annotation.surface: A town is level at the centre of a playground.
annotation.walkthrough: ST(EVEN)AGE. 'Play area' suggests a playground, but it is where a play is acted. Stevenage is a new town in Hertfordshire, north of London.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Stevenage, Britain's first post-war new town, about 30 miles north of London.

entries.clue: Northern location lacks right cooking vessel (8)

indicatorNotes.lacks: lacks means a letter is missing

blocks.note: Stockport, a town near Manchester in northern England
R = right, removed from STOCKPORT

annotation.surface: A place in the north has no proper pan for cooking.
annotation.walkthrough: Stockport is a town in Greater Manchester; take out one R and you have a kitchen pot.
annotation.definitionFit: A stockpot is a large deep pan for simmering stock.

entries.clue: Mammal just keen, we’re told (5,5)

indicatorNotes.we’re told: we're told signals that the words are heard, not read

blocks.note: right = just, fair
to keen is to wail in grief; WAIL sounds like WHALE

annotation.surface: Someone is simply eager, or so we hear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like an adjective (eager) but is the verb for lamenting over the dead, which gives WAIL.
annotation.definitionFit: The right whale is a large baleen whale, so named as the 'right' one to hunt.

entries.clue: Empty gesture, say, to develop slowly (7)

indicatorNotes.Empty: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving the outer letters

blocks.note: GesturE with its inside removed
to state = to say

annotation.surface: A hollow gesture, made say, to let things develop slowly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like the 'for example' signal, but it is the verb, meaning to state.
annotation.definitionFit: To gestate is to carry and develop in the womb, or figuratively to let an idea mature slowly.

entries.clue: Delayed with other people heading west (4)

indicatorNotes.heading west: in an across entry, going west means reading right to left

blocks.note: et al. = and others, from the Latin et alii

annotation.surface: Held up with a group of others travelling west.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' belongs to the wordplay: et al. means 'and others'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a train that is running late has been delayed.

entries.clue: In battle site to the north of Delaware (1,2,4)

indicatorNotes.to the north of: in a down entry, north means above

blocks.note: the Alamo, Texas mission besieged in 1836
DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware

annotation.surface: A battlefield located north of the state of Delaware.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition but is the adjective 'fashionable', as in 'the in crowd'.
annotation.definitionFit: À la mode means fashionable, which is what 'in' means.

entries.clue: Waitress finally put down vegetable (6)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally takes the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the last letter of waitresS
to quash = to suppress, put down

annotation.surface: A waitress at last sets down a vegetable dish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put down' looks like setting a plate on a table, but it means suppress, as in putting down a revolt.
annotation.definitionFit: Squash is a gourd vegetable, such as butternut.

entries.clue: Fundamental programming language (5)

blocks.note: an adjective: at the root, essential
an early 1960s language written for beginners, its name an acronym

annotation.surface: A foundational computer language.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one description, but it is two separate definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Basic means fundamental, and BASIC is a programming language designed for beginners.

entries.clue: Add juice to some cutlets a butcher sent back (5)

indicatorNotes.some: some takes part of the words that follow
indicatorNotes.sent back: sent back means the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: cutlETS A Butcher: the run spans three words, and reads right to left

annotation.surface: Pour gravy over a few cutlets that a butcher had to return.
annotation.walkthrough: The butcher's shop keeps the kitchen picture going; the answer hides backwards across three words.
annotation.definitionFit: To baste is to spoon juices over meat while it cooks.

entries.clue: Friend loses finale after playing game — catastrophe! (9)

indicatorNotes.after: QUAKE comes after the other piece
indicatorNotes.playing: playing means the letters of 'game' are put into play

blocks.note: GAME rearranged
a Quaker belongs to the Religious Society of Friends; drop the last letter R

annotation.surface: A pal drops out of the final after a match, which is a disaster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Friend' has a capital only because it starts the clue; it means a Quaker. 'Finale' suggests the end of a game, but it is the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A megaquake is an enormous earthquake, a catastrophe; the exclamation mark adds drama.

entries.clue: Produced low frame of mind to conserve energy (5)

indicatorNotes.to conserve: to conserve is to keep, so MOOD keeps E inside

blocks.note: mood = frame of mind
E = energy, placed after MOO

annotation.surface: Feeling down, someone saves their energy.
annotation.walkthrough: MOO(E)D. 'Produced low' sounds like feeling depressed; to low is what cattle do, so a cow that lowed mooed.
annotation.definitionFit: To low is to moo, so 'produced low' is mooed.

entries.clue: Craft with a bow and mast fashioned outside entrance to Portsmouth (5,4)

indicatorNotes.fashioned: fashioned means the letters are made into a new shape
indicatorNotes.outside: the rearranged letters go outside P
indicatorNotes.entrance to: the entrance to a word is its first letter

blocks.note: A BOW MAST rearranged; 'and' joins the two
the first letter of Portsmouth, placed after SWAM

annotation.surface: A vessel with bow and mast is built around a Portsmouth dock entrance.
annotation.walkthrough: SWAM(P)BOAT. Portsmouth, the naval port on England's south coast, fits the ship picture, but gives only its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A swamp boat is a flat-bottomed craft, often fan-driven, for shallow wetlands.

entries.clue: Member carrying over a bouquet (5)

indicatorNotes.carrying: carrying means holding inside, so ARM carries O

blocks.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
O = over in cricket scoring, placed after AR
the A as printed, added at the end

annotation.surface: A club member arrives carrying flowers.
annotation.walkthrough: AR(O)M + A. 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, but it is the smell of a wine.
annotation.definitionFit: A wine-tasting sense: the bouquet is the scent rising from the glass, not a bunch of flowers.

entries.clue: Ousted Democrat leaves very upset (7)

indicatorNotes.leaves: leaves means the letter goes out of the word

blocks.note: dejected = very downcast
D = Democrat, removed from DEJECTED

annotation.surface: A Democrat thrown out of office leaves, deeply unhappy.
annotation.walkthrough: The political scene is apt, as the ousted Democrat really is dejected; he is the D that leaves.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe being forcibly removed from a place or post.

entries.clue: Gasp and cries of excitement heard? (6)

indicatorNotes.heard?: heard signals that the answer sounds like the words

blocks.note: 'Whee!' is a cry of excitement; two of them are whees

annotation.surface: A gasp followed by shouts of glee.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the plural of 'whee' is not a real word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a noisy, laboured breath, as an asthmatic makes, is a gasp.
